\title{Criticality of De-Morgan formulae}

\section{Canonical Decision Tree}

We begin by describing an algorithm to construct the canonical decision tree of a De-Morgan formula under a restriction $\rho$. 
The algorithm is based on the Next Variable Function, a sub-routine specifying the next variable to query in the decision tree. 

\paragraph{Next variable function}
\begin{definition} $\NVF(F,\rho)$
Let $F$ be a De-Morgan formula, let $\rho$ be a restriction such that $F|_{\rho}$ is non-constant. 
$\NVF(F,\rho)$ is a sub-routine which takes as input a formula $F$ and a restriction $\rho$ and returns a leaf of its formula tree. 
$\NVF(F,\rho)$ is  defined inductively as follows:
\textbf{Base case}: 
$F$ is a leaf $\ell$, then return $\ell$. (Since $F|\rho$ is non-constant).
\textbf{Recursive step}: Let $F = F_1 \vee F_2$, (the case when $F = F_1 \wedge F_2$ is handled similarly.)
    \begin{itemize}
        \item   if $F_1|_\rho \equiv 0$:
	       return $\NVF(F_2,\rho)$. 
       \item else: 
		  return $\NVF(F_1,\rho)$.
    \end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Canonical Decision Tree $\CDT(F,\rho)$]
\begin{itemize}
    \item If $F|_{\rho} \equiv 0/1$, return a single node labelled 0/1.
\item Else,  let $x_{i_1}$ be the variable corresponding to $\ell_1= \NVF(F,\rho)$, add a node labelled $x_{i_1}$ and for $a \in \{0,1\}$, attach the tree $\CDT(F,\rho(x_{i_1} \to a))$ to this node on the edge labelled $a$ .
\end{itemize}
      
\end{definition}



 
\section{Karchmer-Wigderson Protocol}

\subsection{Karchmer-Wigderson Game} 
It is a two-player game with two players, Alice and Bob, who are given a function $F$ and private inputs. 
Alice receives an input $x$ such that $F(x) = 1$.
Bob receives an input $y$ such that $F(y) = 0$.
\textbf{The Goal:} Alice and Bob want to find an index $i$ such that $x_i  \neq y_i$ . In other words, they want to find a index  where their inputs differ.

\subsection{The Standard Protocol}
For a Boolean formula $F$, the players traverse its formula tree to find the index where the inputs to Alice and Bob differ.

\paragraph{Karchmer-Wigderson Protocol for a Boolean Formula:}

Let us assume \(F\) is represented as a Boolean formula using AND, OR, and NOT gates. The protocol is defined recursively:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Leaf Node (Input Variable):} If $F$ is a single variable $x_i$ , Alice simply sends her bit $x_i$  to Bob. Bob can then determine the differing index.
    \item \textbf{AND Gate:} If $F= G \wedge H$, Alice and Bob first determine which sub-formula ($G$ or $H$) evaluates to 0 on Bob's input $y$. Bob sends a bit to Alice indicating this. They then recursively play the KW game on the chosen sub-formula.
    \item \textbf{OR Gate:} If $F = G \wedge H$,  Alice and Bob first determine which sub-formula ($G$ or $H$) evaluates to 1 on Alice's input *x*. Alice sends a bit to Bob indicating this. They then recursively play the KW game on the chosen sub-formula.
\end{itemize}

$\NVF(F,\rho) = \ell_1$ and 
$\CDT_0^{(a_2, \dots, a_t)}(F,\rho(x_{i_1} \to a_1)) = \ell_2, \dots , \ell_t$.

    \Pr[\CDT_0^{(a)}(F,\rho) &= \ell_1, \dots , \ell_t|\Delta] = \Pr[\NVF(F,\rho) = \ell_1] \cdot \Pr[\CDT_0^{(a_2, \dots, a_t)}(F,\rho(x_{i_1} \to a_1)) = \ell_2, \dots , \ell_t]
\end{align*}
